text: I am selling a $10M luxury residential property in Australia. Which prestige real estate agencies have the strongest track record for high-end home sales?

result.keyword: I am selling a $10M luxury residential property in Australia. Which prestige real estate agencies have the strongest track record for high-end home sales?
result.markdown:
For a \$10 million luxury residential property in Australia, I would shortlist **specialist prestige agencies with a demonstrable record of selling homes at or above your price point**, rather than simply choosing the largest real estate network.

The most important distinction is whether an agency regularly sells \$10 million-plus properties in *your particular market* and has access to qualified high-net-worth buyers, including off-market purchasers.

There isn't a single independently verified national ranking of the best luxury agencies. However, recent reported sales, agent rankings and prestige-market results point to several strong candidates. For example, Kay & Burton has reported a leading share of Melbourne's ultra-prestige market, while Kollosche's Michael Kollosche ranked eighth nationally in the 2026 REB Top 100 Agents list. ## Which agencies would I interview first?

For a \$10 million home, I would start with three agencies that best fit the property's location, then compare their individual agents rather than appointing solely on brand reputation.

| If the property is in… | First agencies to interview |
|--------|--------|
| Sydney, especially the eastern suburbs | Pillinger, Sotheby's International Realty, McGrath |
| Melbourne, especially Toorak or Brighton | Kay & Burton, Marshall White, Sotheby's International Realty |
| Gold Coast | Kollosche, plus a proven local prestige specialist |
| Brisbane | Ray White Collective Luxury, plus established local prestige agents |
| Elsewhere in Australia | A specialist with recent \$5M–\$15M sales in the same local market |


McGrath is also worth considering in Sydney: its latest prestige research tracks the \$10 million-plus segment and provides useful market context for setting a realistic campaign strategy. ## How to establish who really has the strongest track record

Before signing an exclusive agency agreement, ask each shortlisted agent for\:

- **Five comparable settled sales\:** Ideally \$7.5M–\$15M properties in your suburb or a genuinely comparable market, with dates and verifiable sale prices.
- **Sale-to-guide performance\:** Original guide, final selling price and days on market. Ask for examples of properties that did not sell as well as expected, too.
- **Qualified buyer access\:** The number of active, financially qualified buyers who could realistically purchase your particular home.
- **Off-market strategy\:** Whether discreet buyer outreach is appropriate before a full public campaign.
- **Net proceeds and campaign costs\:** Written estimates of commission, photography, styling, advertising, auction costs if applicable, and other expenses.
- **The actual lead agent\:** Who will personally negotiate with buyers, rather than just present the listing pitch.

One important market consideration: CBRE's September 2026 prestige-market survey found that buyer demand had softened, with half of surveyed valuers describing demand in their local markets as soft. This makes evidence of recent comparable sales and a credible pricing strategy especially important. search_results.title: Sunshine Beach lottery mansion sells for $4m below prize value
search_results.description: A retired engineer from Sydney won a luxurious Mediterranean-style mansion in Sunshine Beach, Queensland, through RSL Queensland’s Dream Home Art Union. The property, named Maslina and located at 27 Adams Street, was valued at $13.9 million and included $250,000 in gold and over $400,000 in luxury furnishings. Despite its lavish features and oceanfront location, the winner opted to sell the property to secure his family's financial future. The mansion, originally purchased by the RSL for $13.25 million in April 2025, was recently sold for $10.15 million to local resort managers Geoffrey and Tamara Hussin. Though the sale price was nearly $4 million below its prize value, it still marked a substantial windfall for the grandfather, who had never previously won anything. The three-level home, designed by Paul Clout, features resort-style amenities including a gym, sauna, wine cellar, and ocean views. While the property's unique lottery origin drew wide interest, the winner prioritized helping his family over living in luxury, saying the win gave him a chance to significantly improve the lives of his loved ones.

search_results.title: Longhurst Property launches in Townsville with 50 deals in year one
search_results.description: Longhurst Property, founded by Nathan Longhurst, officially launched as an independent real estate agency in January 2026 after previously operating under the Professionals franchise. Leveraging Mr. Longhurst's international sales experience, the agency quickly gained momentum, completing approximately 50 property transactions within its first year. Specializing in various residential properties, the firm expanded from zero to four staff members. The current Townsville real estate market has shifted due to government tax changes, causing a reduction in investor activity and a rise in owner-occupier buyers. This led to a growing inventory of available homes, increasing from 250-300 to 600-700 properties. Longhurst highlighted the importance of property pricing, presentation, and marketing, emphasizing that the right strategy can turn it into a sellers' market. The agency secured a prominent office location at 219 Charters Towers Rd, Mysterton—a former book shop and Asian supermarket—which was purchased for $560,000 and renovated. The property offers high visibility and includes four onsite parking spaces, supporting the firm’s operational needs.

search_results.title: Mermaid Waters termite-damaged waterfront sells for $2.648m
search_results.description: A termite-damaged waterfront property at 46 Markeri St, Mermaid Waters, sold for $2.648 million after a competitive auction involving three bidders. The 1148 sqm estate offers 62m of exclusive water frontage and was owned for 30 years by two sisters-in-law. Due to the property's extensive maintenance needs and structural damage—caused by Queensland’s climate including mould, wood rot, and termites—it was marketed transparently as a renovator’s opportunity or potential knockdown project. Real estate agent Gypsea Youngsmith of Kollosche said they received strong interest during a three-week campaign, with 55 inquiries and 26 inspections. A local buyer, already engaged with the agency, purchased the dual-occupancy home which features five bedrooms, five bathrooms, two kitchens, two laundries, and amenities such as a private boat ramp and waterside pool. Estimated rental income is between $2000 and $2200 per week. Building designer Jayson Pate was consulted to help illustrate the block’s redevelopment potential. The successful sale reflects continuing confidence in the Gold Coast market despite a slight downturn, with Mermaid Waters' median house prices up 21.5% over the past year to $2.4 million.

search_results.title: Gold Coast luxury property defies downturn as Sydney buyers move in
search_results.description: Despite a nationwide property downturn that has reverted prices and sales to 2023 levels, the Gold Coast luxury real estate market remains resilient. This strength is attributed to a limited housing supply, robust internal migration, and affluent buyers—particularly from Sydney—seeking better value. Michael Kollosche, managing director of Kollosche, highlights how high-end Gold Coast apartments, priced between $25,000 and $35,000 per square metre, offer better value compared to Sydney's $120,000 per square metre rates. Notable recent sales include an $11.5 million penthouse purchase by a European investor. According to Colliers, Gold Coast property prices have surged 84% since 2021, surpassing Brisbane and Greater Brisbane. Analyst Michael Matusik notes a shift from investment properties to owner-occupied beachfront homes, as the city attracts wealthy buyers post-pandemic. Downsizing among affluent homeowners along Hedges Avenue is driving demand for luxurious, smaller residences in the same prime locations. This demographic shift is shaping a robust, high-end market insulated from broader sectoral declines.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

search_results.title: Hamilton Grove: $1.2b luxury towers break ground in Brisbane
search_results.description: Wentworth Equities has commenced construction on the $1.2 billion Hamilton Grove precinct in Brisbane, marked by an official sod-turning ceremony attended by government representatives. Located in the 304-hectare Northshore Hamilton Priority Development Area, the ambitious project includes three luxury residential towers comprising 292 apartments, a 196-room five-star hotel, 3,000 square meters of retail space, and a vibrant public precinct. Executive Chairman Sameh Ibrahim emphasized the project's historic significance and its aim to redefine apartment living by offering suburban-style space and character in an urban setting. Contractor Mainland Civil, known for its work on other high-profile Brisbane projects such as Queens Wharf and Infinity Tower, is leading construction. The Queensland Government is supporting the broader development of Hamilton Northshore with a $154 million infrastructure investment, aiming to add more than $14 billion to the local economy upon completion. Hamilton Grove has drawn strong buyer interest since its April launch, and future development phases, including the hotel, are already in planning. The project aspires to set a new standard for luxury living in Brisbane with its standout “sky homes” serving as its centerpiece.

search_results.title: Aria's Sanctuary Residences: $519m sold before public launch
search_results.description: Aria Property Group has reported a record-breaking pre-launch success for its Sanctuary Residences project in South Brisbane, achieving $519 million in apartment sales, making it Queensland’s largest apartment launch to date. Remarkably, sales were made without any public advertising, focusing on high-end three and four-bedroom apartments priced from $2.72 million and $4.01 million. Of the 231 apartments available in the first tower, only 86 remain unsold. Designed for buyers seeking spacious, luxurious homes without downsizing, the project has attracted strong interest. The development at 164-190 Melbourne Street includes restoration of two heritage buildings and features expansive amenities such as a wellness club, rooftop bar, and 2.9-meter ceilings. It is part of a larger master-planned precinct with public parks, laneways, and retail spaces. The first tower is set to complete by mid-to-late 2029, aligning with Brisbane's preparation for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. This overwhelming response reflects growing demand for high-quality apartment living in Brisbane. The remaining units will be publicly released on October 19, with potential price increases expected.

search_results.title: Graya breaks ground on Brisbane's most expensive house in New Farm
search_results.description: Celebrity developers Graya have commenced construction on a lavish mansion dubbed “Ivory,” on an exclusive riverfront block in New Farm, Brisbane, purchased by Chemist Warehouse boss Jeff Wasley and his wife Tanya for a record-breaking $25 million in 2025. Designed and built by Graya over 11 months, the home is expected to be worth between $40-$50 million upon completion. The 688 sqm site was previously owned by Graya co-founder Rob Gray and originally intended as his personal residence before it was sold for a $16.5 million profit. Ivory features a five-storey design including high-end amenities such as a luxury car showroom with river views, resort-style pools, rooftop entertainment areas, a wellness center, state-of-the-art golf simulator, and a master suite with 10-meter wardrobes. The house boasts a sleek, neutral finish with white, curved terraces and mushroom-style pillars. Located between New Farm Park and the Story Bridge, the property offers panoramic views of Brisbane’s skyline. This milestone build reflects Graya’s continued influence in Brisbane's luxury real estate market. The Wasleys had previously acquired another Graya-built home in Hamilton for $12.5 million.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Inside Katanga: Hamilton's grand 1884 riverfront estate for sale
search_results.description: Katanga, a prestigious 1884 riverfront estate in Hamilton, Brisbane, is now on the market after an extensive transformation blending historical charm with modern luxury. Located at 25 Langside Road on a 1113 m² plot, the home has been thoughtfully redesigned by Twohill & James, maintaining its original heritage while introducing contemporary, lift-connected living across three levels. Current owners Sam and Brad Hopper, who previously owned a prominent Sunshine Beach property, sought to honor the home's history through elegant updates, including Calacatta Viola marble and travertine finishes. The residence features five ensuite bedrooms, including a luxurious parents' retreat, a self-contained guest wing, and numerous leisure amenities such as a gym, sauna, cinema, alfresco terrace, wet-edge pool, and heated spa. The impressive kitchen and entertaining areas integrate seamlessly with modern family functionality, while features such as a 10-car garage, dual EV chargers, and private office further enhance its appeal. With its sweeping river views and seamless blend of old and new, Katanga is a rare Brisbane gem now ready for new owners.

search_results.title: Hawk star Jarman Impey lists Brighton East home for $2.1m
search_results.description: AFL star Jarman Impey of the Hawthorn Hawks has listed his Brighton East home for sale at $1.95m–$2.1m following a successful footy season. Impey played a key role in helping the Hawks finish fourth and reach the preliminary final in 2026, and was named on the All Australian team. He previously played 75 games for Port Adelaide before moving to Hawthorn in 2018, reaching a total of 169 matches with them. He is also known for his long-standing representation in the Indigenous All-Stars team. The property, located near Dendy Park, features a spacious layout suitable for families or professionals, with four bedrooms, a Miele kitchen, dual living zones, and convenient access to local amenities. Impey attributes the nearby facilities like the athletics track to his maintained fitness, citing its grass surface as ideal for AFL training. Impey and his wife Annabelle hope the next owners enjoy the home as much as they did with their 17-month-old son Zion. The sale is handled by Kay & Burton's Matthew Pillios, who praises the home’s location and lifestyle appeal.

search_results.title: Fashion retail mogul Dean Mintz lists luxury Toorak mansion
search_results.description: Dean Mintz, the reclusive entrepreneur and founder of luxury fashion e-retailer Cettire, has listed his opulent Toorak mansion for sale. Valued at $729 million in 2024, Mintz launched Cettire in 2017, offering designer brands like Prada, Gucci, and Fendi at discounted prices. He profited over $300 million from selling shares after listing the company on the ASX in 2020. Mintz purchased the five-bedroom mansion in 2021 for $14.5 million. The home, marketed by Melbourne Sotheby's International Realty, boasts high-end features including a six-car garage, heated pool, wine cellar with tasting room, elevator, and advanced security. Designed by Flack Studio and architect Richard Blight, the residence features luxury finishes such as Italian stone kitchens, hand-carved oak staircase, Murano Venini chandeliers, and heated travertine floors. Additional highlights include Gaggenau and Miele appliances, a second kitchen, four ensuite bedrooms, and advanced home automation systems. Located on a court in Toorak, the home offers 40 meters of north-facing garden frontage and has been described as a "modernist masterwork" and a standout in Melbourne's elite real estate market.

search_results.title: Grand home of real estate legend Di Jones sells above guide
search_results.description: A three-bedroom apartment formerly owned by late real estate pioneer Di Jones has sold for $7.7 million, surpassing its guide price by $200,000. Located on level nine of The Residence in Darlinghurst, Sydney, and overlooking Hyde Park, the apartment attracted 167 buyer inquiries, 64 inspections, and competitive bidding from three buyers. The successful sale also marks a relaunch of Kim Jones & Co, led by Di Jones' daughter Kim, who had previously excelled in Byron Bay. Di Jones, who revolutionized Sydney real estate by founding its first female-driven agency in 1992, purchased the property in 2011 for $4 million. The apartment will now serve as a city residence for a couple from Wagga Wagga. Another property tied to Di Jones, a two-bedroom Woollahra unit owned by artist Sally Aurisch, is also drawing interest ahead of its November 10 auction with hopes of fetching $3 million. Despite wider market softening due to higher interest rates and cost-of-living pressures, the auction event hosted by Damien Cooley saw 11 out of 12 properties sold, with several surpassing their reserve prices.

search_results.title: Fire-ravaged Sydney home sparks hot auction
search_results.description: Despite its fire-damaged condition, a former Homes NSW housing commission property at 19 Robertson Street, Merrylands attracted significant interest at auction. With six registered bidders and competitive bidding, the home sold for $1.061 million—above its $1.050 million reserve. This is notable considering broader trends of low auction activity in Sydney, driven by rising interest rates and market uncertainty. Chief Auctioneer Ben Mitchell noted such demand reflects buyer interest in properties with potential, especially near the $1 million price point. Agent Soon Tee highlighted the property's appeal due to its 682 sqm land size and potential for redevelopment, with the buyer intending to construct a house and granny flat. Overall affordability under $1.5 million remains active. Despite overall lower auction clearance rates in Sydney, which sat at 37% in early October due to economic pressures, other high-profile sales also occurred. A Randwick home sold for $3.86 million, and a five-bedroom Bronte property exceeded its reserve by almost $1 million, selling for $12.12 million. These successful sales suggest selective resilience in the Sydney property market.

search_results.title: Wealthy Aussie family bears brunt of brutal housing downturn
search_results.description: Australia's luxury property market is experiencing a significant downturn, highlighted by dramatic declines in high-profile home sales. A four-bedroom home in Flinders, Victoria, originally offered at $10.25 million, eventually sold for $7.8 million after 305 days on the market. Similarly, Rothesay, a six-bedroom mansion in Balmain East, Sydney, recently sold for $12.8 million—down nearly 35% from its $19.76 million price in 2022. The owner, businessman Devesh Mishra, had declared bankruptcy following the collapse of his firms, prompting a mortgagee-in-possession sale. Real estate agents cite high interest rates, low buyer inquiries, and financial instability—including inflation and global conflict—as key drivers of the market slump. Experts from Cotality Research and AMP predict property value declines of up to 15%, surpassing earlier forecasts and marking the steepest post-war price fall in Australia. National home values have dropped 5.2% since March, with capital cities like Sydney and Melbourne seeing even steeper declines. Agents suggest deferring property sales until after upcoming elections, hoping for market stabilization.

Crown profit slump as casino makes bet on Melbourne bounce back
search_results.description:
Crown, the Australian casino operator now owned by Blackstone, reported a sharp profit decline to $67.1 million for the past fiscal year – down 52.8% from 2025. This drop follows a long period of regulatory scrutiny, litigation, and market challenges. Revenue grew slightly by 2.8% to $2.91 billion, with modest gains in Melbourne (4.7%) and Perth (2.5%), and a stronger 8.7% rise in Sydney. However, Crown’s financials remain strained, relying on a $739 million interest-free loan from Blackstone and posting a net liability of $329 million.

Despite ongoing pressure from tighter regulations, cashless gaming, higher taxes, and reduced international high-roller traffic, Crown is pushing forward with a $200 million revamp of its Melbourne flagship – the first major investment since Blackstone’s $9 billion acquisition in 2022. The overhaul focuses on new dining and entertainment options rather than gaming expansion. Sydney and Perth properties are also receiving upgrades. Crown received regulatory clearance to retain its casino licenses in WA, Victoria, and NSW, contrasting with rival Star Entertainment’s continued troubles. While macroeconomic conditions and rising living costs pose consumer risks, Crown aims to build a sustainable, long-term business through diversified entertainment offerings.

## How to establish who really has the strongest track record

Before signing an exclusive agency agreement, ask each shortlisted agent for\:

- **Five comparable settled sales\:** Ideally \$7.5M–\$15M properties in your suburb or a genuinely comparable market, with dates and verifiable sale prices.
- **Sale-to-guide performance\:** Original guide, final selling price and days on market. Ask for examples of properties that did not sell as well as expected, too.
- **Qualified buyer access\:** The number of active, financially qualified buyers who could realistically purchase your particular home.
- **Off-market strategy\:** Whether discreet buyer outreach is appropriate before a full public campaign.
- **Net proceeds and campaign costs\:** Written estimates of commission, photography, styling, advertising, auction costs if applicable, and other expenses.
- **The actual lead agent\:** Who will personally negotiate with buyers, rather than just present the listing pitch.

One important market consideration: CBRE's September 2026 prestige-market survey found that buyer demand had softened, with half of surveyed valuers describing demand in their local markets as soft. This makes evidence of recent comparable sales and a credible pricing strategy especially important.
